title: Rubio Meets Syrian FM al-Shaibani in Antalya in High-Level US-Syria Talks; Sanctions Relief Confirmed
detail: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio held a trilateral meeting with Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shaibani and Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on the margins of a NATO foreign ministers meeting in Antalya, Turkey. The meeting represents one of the highest-level US-Syria diplomatic engagements in approximately 15 years. Rubio confirmed the Trump administration would proceed with comprehensive sanctions relief for Syria, building on earlier waivers granted in early 2025. The meeting also addressed Syria's accession as the 90th member of the D-ISIS Coalition and ongoing US efforts to locate missing American citizens in Syria. Turkey's facilitation of the talks underscores Ankara's central role as a key broker for the Syrian transitional government's international rehabilitation. The Antalya trilateral reflects the alignment between US, Turkish, and Syrian transitional government interests in countering residual ISIS presence and stabilizing the post-Assad transition.

media.caption: Rubio meets Syrian FM al-Shaibani in Antalya, confirms comprehensive sanctions relief process

title: UN Security Council: Syria Humanitarian Appeal Only 16% Funded, WFP Halves Food Assistance
detail: UN Under-Secretary-General for Humanitarian Affairs Tom Fletcher briefed the UN Security Council on Syria's severe humanitarian funding gap. Key findings: 15.6 million people — two-thirds of Syria's total population — require humanitarian assistance. The $2.9 billion 2026 Syria humanitarian appeal has received only $480 million, representing just 16% of required funding and leaving a $2.4 billion gap. The World Food Programme has been forced to cut emergency food assistance by 50%, reducing beneficiaries from 1.3 million to 650,000 people. Since early March 2026, over 390,000 people entered Syria from Lebanon (90,000 since April's Security Council briefing), adding pressure to already strained services. Economic conditions are deteriorating for ordinary Syrians: diesel prices are up 17%, electricity costs have risen several hundred percent in some areas, and government-subsidized bread loaf sizes have been reduced by 12%. Despite the political transition, Syria's humanitarian situation remains critical and chronically underfunded.

media.caption: UN Security Council briefed on Syria — humanitarian appeal only 16% funded, WFP cuts food aid by 50%
